newsitem.title: HONG KONG: K. Wah Int'l in group restructuring.
newsitem.headline: K. Wah Int'l in group restructuring.

text.p: K. Wah International Holdings Ltd said on Monday it plans to streamline the group's business by injecting two construction material units into concrete pipes maker International Pipe Ltd.

International Pipe, a 63.8 percent owned unit of K. Wah, has agreed to pay HK$610 million for Taksin Profits Ltd and High Regard Investments Ltd owned by K. Wah subsidiary Sutimar Enterprises Ltd, K. Wah said in a statement.
The consideration will be satisfied by the issue of 512.61 million new shares in International Pipe at HK$1.19 each to K.Wah, it added.
K. Wah said about 238.21 million consideration shares will be allotted to K. Wah shareholders on a one-for-four basis with the remaining 274.39 million shares issued to Sutimar.

It also agreed to assign to International Pipe a HK$306 million unsecured and non-interest bearing shareholder loan owed by Taksin and High Regard in exchange for a HK$306 million four percent convertible note issued by International Pipe.
The agreements are subject to the approval of International Pipe's independent shareholders, K. Wah said.
Taksin is an investment holding company with subsidiaries engaged in quarry operations and in the production, sale and distribution of construction materials in Hong Kong and China's Zhuhai zone.
High Regard has interests in six joint venture companies in Guangzhou and Shanghai which undertake most of the group's construction materials business in China.

The consideration represents a price earnings multiple of 8.7 times the combined net profit after notional interest on shareholders loans of Taksin and High Regard of HK$70.19 million for the financial year of March 31, 1996, K. Wah said.
The combined net asset value of the two companies was HK$171.53 million on March 31, 1996.
After the restructuring, K. Wah group said it would focus its resources on property development and investment.
